approach: Replace the single `checks` job in ci.yml with a small `gate` job (D121 fingerprint, lookup, decide), parallel `fmt`, `clippy` and a 6-shard `test` matrix, a `pass` job that writes the D121 marker only when every check succeeded, and a final `ci` job (`if: always()`) that fails unless every needed job succeeded (or was skipped because the gate reused a pass). Add `xtask test-shard <k> <n> [--dry-run]` in a new `xtask/src/shard.rs`: it lists workspace test units from `cargo metadata --no-deps`, sorts them, gives unit i to shard `i % n`, and runs `cargo test --locked -p <pkg> <selector>` per unit. A new `xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs` reads ci.yml and checks the shards form an exact partition. The check is split in two. A shape rule checks the matrix list and the command. A pure `check_cover(shards, oracle)` compares the shards' units with an oracle from `cargo metadata`. Negative cases hit each layer separately, including cases that pass the shape rule and break only the cover. The oracle is cross-checked against files on disk (every `src/lib.rs`, `tests/*.rs`, `src/main.rs`, `src/bin/*.rs`). policy.rs is re-pointed at the new job names because it would otherwise fail. No new crates, so Cargo.lock should be unchanged.

decisions.choice: A separate `gate` job runs fingerprint, lookup and decide. `fmt`, `clippy` and `test` declare `needs: gate` and `if: needs.gate.outputs.skip != 'true'`. A separate `pass` job (default success() condition, needs gate, fmt, clippy, test) builds xtask with stable cargo, runs `ci-cache mark ci-pass "$FINGERPRINT" --outcome "$OUTCOME"` and saves `ci-pass`.
decisions.reason: The fingerprint and lookup run once, not eight times. The marker is written only when every check job succeeded, because a failed or skipped need skips `pass` under the default condition. On a reused pass the compute jobs and `pass` are skipped. Mark and save steps stay free of always()/failure(), as the existing policy test requires.

rejected.option: Run the whole D121 prelude in every job
rejected.why: Eight fingerprint builds and lookups, and eight jobs each deciding whether to write one marker, so a partial pass could be saved.

rejected.option: Put the marker step inside the `ci` job
rejected.why: `ci` would then need a checkout and an xtask build before reporting, so it would lag behind the checks.

rejected.option: Pass the xtask binary between jobs with an artifact action
rejected.why: Needs two more action SHAs that cannot be verified here; the pass job's rebuild is off the critical path.

decisions.choice: The `ci` job needs [gate, fmt, clippy, test], runs `if: always()`, and a shell step reads `needs.*.result`. `gate` must be success. If `gate.outputs.skip == 'true'`, fmt, clippy and test must all be `skipped`; otherwise all three must be `success`. Anything else exits 1. `ci` does not need `pass`.
decisions.reason: One check name says whether a commit is green, including the reused-pass case. A cancelled job, or one skipped by mistake, cannot pass. A marker-write fault is an infrastructure problem and should not turn a commit red. The cost, that `ci` can finish before `pass` writes the marker, is stated as a known effect in the CHANGELOG and design doc (see decision 8).

rejected.option: Let `ci` need `pass`
rejected.why: On a failed check `pass` is skipped, so `ci` needs special cases, and a marker-write failure would fail the required check.

rejected.option: Treat `skipped` as success in `ci`
rejected.why: A job skipped by a broken `needs` or `if` would pass silently.

decisions.choice: Shard unit = workspace test target. For each workspace member take targets with `test: true` and kind lib, rlib, proc-macro, bin or test, giving selectors `--lib`, `--bin <name>`, `--test <name>`. Add a `--doc` unit for each lib target with `doctest: true`. Sort by (package, selector). Unit i goes to shard `i % n`. Shards are 0-based.
decisions.reason: Mirrors what `cargo test --workspace` runs: examples and benches have `test=false` and are excluded, and doctests run once per package. Index-modulo over a sorted list is deterministic and needs no cost data.

rejected.option: Shard by individual test name from `cargo test -- --list`
rejected.why: Compiles everything to plan, takes more code, and name filters can misselect on overlapping names.

rejected.option: Weight units by source size and deal out greedily
rejected.why: Better balance but more code and a split that depends on file contents; a follow-up if the throughput review shows poor balance.

rejected.option: Use a sharding tool such as cargo-nextest partitioning
rejected.why: Needs a new pinned tool and changes how doctests run. Buy-first call recorded in a shard.rs comment: cargo metadata plus cargo test meet the need.

decisions.choice: `xtask test-shard` runs one `cargo test --locked -p <pkg> <selector>` per unit, in order, keeps going after a failure, then exits non-zero naming the failed units. `--dry-run` prints one `<pkg> <selector>` line per unit and runs nothing. `ci()` stays for local use. A comment in shard.rs and the risk list note that per-unit `-p` runs may resolve features differently from one `--workspace` run (resolver 3 unifies over the selected packages), so the tests can run against a slightly different build; the throughput review should watch for extra dependency recompiles.
decisions.reason: Cargo cannot attach a different target selector to each `-p`, so one invocation per unit runs exactly the selected units. Continuing shows every failing test file in one run. `--dry-run` gives the partition test and local users the selection without compiling.

rejected.option: A single `cargo test -p a -p b --lib --test x`
rejected.why: Target flags apply to every selected package, so the selection would be wrong or empty.

rejected.option: Group a shard's units by package into one invocation
rejected.why: Fewer invocations, but it does not remove the feature-resolution difference (the selection is still per package, not workspace-wide) and it adds code. Left as a follow-up if the review shows recompile cost.

decisions.choice: The partition test has three layers. (a) `parse_workflow(text) -> Result<(Vec<u32> shard_list, u32 n), String>` reads `shard: [..]` in the `test` job and the single `test-shard ${{ matrix.shard }} <n>` command, using regexes. It requires the list to be exactly 0..n, with the command once and n equal to the list length. (b) `shard_units(list, n)` runs `xtask test-shard k n --dry-run` per listed k. (c) A pure `check_cover(shards: &[Vec<String>], oracle: &BTreeSet<String>) -> Result<(), String>` fails with the unit named if a unit appears in two shards, is missing from all, or appears in a shard but not in the oracle. `check_partition(text)` calls (a), (b), then (c). Negative cases: shape mutations on ci.yml text (drop shard, duplicate shard, change n) test (a); and cover-only cases test (c) directly with the shape rule already passed. The cover-only cases are one unit removed from a shard, one unit copied into a second shard, and an oracle with one extra unit. Each is asserted Err with the unit named in the message. A sanity positive case asserts (c) returns Ok for the real shards.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2: the earlier negatives were all rejected by the shape rule before the comparison ran, so an always-Ok comparison would not have been caught. Splitting (c) out as a pure function lets the test feed it shards that are well-formed but wrong. There is no YAML crate in Cargo.lock, and adding one needs network access and changes Cargo.lock; `regex` is already a dev-dependency.

rejected.option: Only mutate ci.yml text
rejected.why: Every text mutation changes the matrix shape, so none reach the cover comparison.

rejected.option: Add a YAML crate as a dev-dependency
rejected.why: Changes Cargo.lock and needs network for one fixed-shape matrix.

rejected.option: Use the output of `test-shard` as the oracle
rejected.why: Checks the splitter against itself and misses a unit dropped from the enumeration.

decisions.choice: The test oracle is computed in ci_shards.rs from `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 --locked` and encodes cargo's documented target rules (test=true targets of kind lib/rlib/proc-macro/bin/test, plus one doctest per doctest-enabled lib), written separately from shard.rs. A comment says why `cargo test --workspace --no-run` inside the test was rejected: it compiles the whole workspace inside a test and prints artifact paths, not stable target names. The oracle is additionally cross-checked against the filesystem: for each workspace member dir, `src/lib.rs` implies a `--lib` unit, each `tests/*.rs` file implies a `--test <stem>`, `src/main.rs` implies a `--bin <package name>`, and each `src/bin/*.rs` implies a `--bin <stem>`. Each of these must appear in the oracle. A separate test fails with the missing entry named.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3: a shared mistake about what cargo runs would otherwise go unnoticed. The filesystem check is independent of the `test`/`doctest` flags in metadata, and it covers the case where the workspace has no overrides today. The test lists, and the comment records, that target-name overrides in Cargo.toml would require updating the check.

rejected.option: Run `cargo test --workspace --no-run` and parse its output as the oracle
rejected.why: Slow inside a test, recompiles the workspace, and output is artifact paths rather than target selectors.

rejected.option: Only comment on the shared rule
rejected.why: A comment documents the risk but does not detect it; the filesystem cross-check is small.

decisions.choice: Per-job target cache keys `target-fmt-`, `target-clippy-`, `target-test-` with the existing restore-key shape. The `test` shards share one key and only shard 0 saves it, on the default branch only. Toolchain and registry keys and the default-branch-only save rule are unchanged.
decisions.reason: Different jobs build different artifacts, so one key would let them overwrite each other. Six shards saving one key race and warn; dependency artifacts, the bulk of the cache, are identical across shards.

rejected.option: One target key per shard
rejected.why: Six large entries against the repository cache quota.

rejected.option: One shared `target-checks-` key
rejected.why: Collisions between the artifacts clippy and test produce.

decisions.choice: Add `timeout-minutes` to every job, including the unchanged `history`, `attribution` and `pr-head` jobs. Values are ceilings (about 30 for fmt, clippy and each shard; smaller for gate, pass and ci), not measurements.
decisions.reason: Criterion 1 requires it on every job; a timeout does not change what those jobs check.

rejected.option: Leave the three untouched jobs without a timeout
rejected.why: Violates criterion 1.

decisions.choice: Leave `EARLY_RUN_JOB` (crates/athena-core/src/gh/early.rs, "fmt, clippy, tests") untouched. Record in the CHANGELOG entry and in docs/design/ci-routing.md, as a KNOWN EFFECT of this change, that `land`'s early-run wait finds no check run with the old name and ends at once, so a landing run can miss the cached pass until the follow-up lands. The follow-up note says the constant should name the job that writes the marker (`pass`), not `ci`, because `ci` does not need `pass` and can finish before the marker is saved; alternatively `ci` could be made to wait for `pass`. The name `ci` is kept for the required check.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 5. The crate and its fixtures (gh/tests.rs lines 1228, 1281, 1377 per the earlier reading) are outside the listed files. Saying `ci` is the wrong target would send the follow-up in the wrong direction, because renaming to `ci` would still race the marker write.

rejected.option: Change the constant to "ci" here
rejected.why: Out of file scope, edits test fixtures, and still races the `pass` job.

rejected.option: Keep a job named "fmt, clippy, tests"
rejected.why: Contradicts the requested single `ci` check name.

decisions.choice: Modify xtask/tests/policy.rs only to re-point its two D121 tests from the single job to the new `gate`, compute and `pass` jobs, via `job_steps(job_id)` replacing `checks_job_steps()`. List it in the files with that reason.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 1 and 6. policy.rs lines 523-529 locate the job by `    name: fmt, clippy, tests` and end the slice at `\n  history:`. Both break once `checks` is replaced, so `cargo test` would fail (criterion 5). The file is under `xtask/`, which the request lists as a deliverable path. The brief's deliverable list omits it, so the plan states the reason and keeps the edit limited to what the layout change forces.

rejected.option: Leave policy.rs unchanged
rejected.why: Its tests would fail on the new ci.yml.

rejected.option: Delete the D121 policy tests
rejected.why: Loses enforcement of the pass-marker rule (mechanism default); re-pointing keeps every assertion that still applies.

files.purpose: Governance file, listed as a deliverable. Replace `checks` with gate, fmt, clippy, a 6-shard `test` matrix, pass and `ci`. Add timeout-minutes to every job. Use per-job target cache keys. Update header comments, including that the new run time is unmeasured. Leave history, attribution and pr-head otherwise unchanged. Keep every `uses:` pinned to its current 40-hex SHA.

`test-shard <k> <n> [--dry-run]`: reads cargo metadata, `plan_units`, `select`, `parse_args`, `command`. Comments record the buy-first call and the feature-resolution caveat. Unit tests run on a metadata fixture.
Add `mod shard;`, the `test-shard` dispatch, the usage line, and updated module docs; `ci()` stays for local use.

Partition test over ci.yml: `parse_workflow`, `check_cover`, `check_partition`, shape and cover-only negative cases, oracle with filesystem cross-check, test-shard n=6/n=1 equality and bad arguments, workflow job/timeout/ci-gate/pinned-action/cache tests.

Required by the layout change, though not in the brief's deliverable list (it is under `xtask/`, which the request lists). Its D121 tests find the job by `    name: fmt, clippy, tests` and end the slice at `\n  history:`; both break when `checks` is replaced. Replace `checks_job_steps` with `job_steps(job_id)` and re-point the two tests at the gate, compute and pass jobs, keeping every assertion that still applies. No other change.
Update the package description to mention `test-shard`. No new dependency.

Unreleased entry: parallel jobs, shard matrix, `ci` gate, `pass` job, `xtask test-shard`, partition test, required-check rename, stale `EARLY_RUN_JOB` as a known effect, and run time not yet measured.

Update the CI job description (~lines 53 and 75). Add a short section on the parallel layout, sharding and the `pass`/`ci` split. State that the run time is to be measured by the throughput review. State the `EARLY_RUN_JOB` follow-up (target the marker-writing job).

steps: Read the rest of the D121 policy test (xtask/tests/policy.rs around lines 520-630), xtask/src/ci_cache.rs (`check` writes `skip` to GITHUB_OUTPUT) and the test patterns in xtask/tests/fingerprint.rs. Note every assertion in policy.rs that must survive the move to the new jobs.

Create xtask/src/shard.rs. Define `Unit { package, selector }` with a sort key. `plan_units(&serde_json::Value) -> Result<Vec<Unit>>` takes members from `packages`, keeps targets with `test: true` and kind lib, rlib, proc-macro, bin or test, and adds a `--doc` unit for each lib target with `doctest: true`. `select(&[Unit], k, n)` returns units with index % n == k over the sorted list. `parse_args` takes `<k> <n> [--dry-run]` and rejects n==0, k>=n and non-numbers with a message. Add comments for the buy-first call (cargo metadata and cargo test, no sharding tool) and the per-unit `-p` feature-resolution caveat.

In shard.rs add `command(args, root)`. It runs `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 --locked` in the repo root, plans and selects. With `--dry-run` it prints `<pkg> <selector>` per line. Otherwise it runs `cargo test --locked -p <pkg> <selector>` per unit using the existing `run` helper pattern, keeps going after a failure, and returns an error listing failed units. A shard with no units prints a note and succeeds. Add unit tests on a hand-written metadata fixture: examples and benches excluded; bin and test selectors; doctest=false lib; selection over n=1, 6 and n greater than the unit count is disjoint and complete; argument errors.

Edit xtask/src/main.rs: add `mod shard;`, `Some("test-shard") => shard::command(&args[1..], &repo_root())`, `shard::USAGE` in the usage text, and update the module doc (CI now calls `test-shard`; `ci` is kept for local use). Update the xtask/Cargo.toml description.

Rewrite .github/workflows/ci.yml. The header describes the layout, the D121 flow (gate, compute jobs, pass, ci), the cache rules, and says the new run time is not measured here and is for the throughput review (the 16 minutes is the labelled D125 baseline; timeouts are ceilings). Jobs: `gate` (checkout, fingerprint, lookup, decide; job `outputs` skip/fingerprint/key; timeout; a step reporting a reused pass). `fmt`, `clippy` and `test` (`needs: gate`, `if: needs.gate.outputs.skip != 'true'`, timeout; `test` has `strategy: {fail-fast: false, matrix: {shard: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]}}`). Each runs checkout, three cache restores with `target-fmt-/target-clippy-/target-test-` keys, the outcome report, `./setup.sh --ci`, then `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, or `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- test-shard ${{ matrix.shard }} 6`, then default-branch-only saves (the test job saves only on shard 0). `pass` (needs gate, fmt, clippy, test; checkout; `cargo +stable build --locked -q -p xtask`; `ci-cache mark ci-pass "$FINGERPRINT" --outcome "$OUTCOME"` with OUTCOME computed from the three results; `cache/save` of `ci-pass` with the gate's key). `ci` (name `ci`, needs gate/fmt/clippy/test, `if: always()`, a shell step over `needs.*.result`). Add `timeout-minutes` to history, attribution and pr-head with no other change. Keep every `uses:` at its current SHA.

Create xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs. Helpers read ci.yml, split job blocks, run xtask via CARGO_BIN_EXE_xtask, and build the oracle from `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 --locked`. The oracle code carries the comment on cargo's documented target rules and why `cargo test --workspace --no-run` was rejected. Write `parse_workflow(text)` for shape checks, a pure `check_cover(shards, oracle)` for missing, duplicated, extra and unknown units, and `check_partition(text)` that calls both after running `--dry-run` per shard. Tests: the real ci.yml passes; shape mutations fail (drop shard, duplicate shard, change n); cover-only negatives call `check_cover` directly (a unit removed, a unit copied to a second shard, an extra oracle unit, a shard unit absent from the oracle) and each error names the unit; a positive control for `check_cover`; `oracle_matches_files_on_disk`; `test-shard` n=6 and n=1 equal the oracle; bad arguments exit non-zero; `workflow_jobs_*` with mutations; `workflow_actions_are_pinned`; `workflow_caches` (each compute job restores the three caches).

Edit xtask/tests/policy.rs: replace `checks_job_steps` with `job_steps(job_id)` (slice from `\n  <id>:\n` to the next two-space-indent job). Re-point the lookup test to the gate job (fingerprint < lookup < decide, the lookup is cache/restore keyed by the fingerprint, the report step carries the skip condition). Assert that each compute job has `needs: gate` and the skip condition and that its toolchain restore comes after the gate. Re-point the pass-marker test to `pass` (mark then save, no status override, no default-branch condition, OUTCOME from the results). Keep the per-job shared-cache saves default-branch-only. Grep docs/enforcement.md for the test names and update it only if it names them.

Update CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased) and docs/design/ci-routing.md: the layout, `test-shard` with an example (`cargo run -p xtask -- test-shard 0 6`) and `--dry-run`, the `ci` check name and that `fmt, clippy, tests` no longer exists, the `pass` job, the known `EARLY_RUN_JOB` effect and its follow-up (name the marker-writing job), and that nothing about the new run time is measured here. Check that no word from the `boundary_words()` scan or email-like text is added.
Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p xtask` and `cargo test --locked`. Confirm Cargo.lock is unchanged.

risks.risk: The `ci` job could report green when a needed job was skipped or cancelled, or red on a legitimately reused pass.
risks.mitigation: workflow_jobs tests assert the step exits non-zero unless every need is success (or skipped when `gate.skip == 'true'`), with text-mutation negatives. A final read of the shell logic covers the cancelled, failure and skipped values.

risks.risk: The D121 marker could be written after a partial failure.
risks.mitigation: The `pass` job has the default success() condition and needs all four jobs. The policy test forbids always/failure/cancelled on the mark and save steps. `mark` writes only for outcome `success`, computed from all three results.

risks.risk: The shard split could drop or repeat a test target (doctests, a bin sharing a name with a lib), and a mistake about cargo's target rules could be shared by shard.rs and the oracle.
risks.mitigation: The cover check is a separate pure function, with cover-only negative cases showing it rejects missing, duplicated, extra and unknown units. The oracle is written independently of shard.rs and cross-checked against `src/lib.rs`, `tests/*.rs`, `src/main.rs` and `src/bin/*.rs` on disk.

risks.risk: Running `cargo test -p <pkg>` once per unit may resolve dependency features differently from one `cargo test --workspace` (resolver 3 unifies over the selected packages). That can compile extra copies of shared dependencies and run tests on a slightly different build.
risks.mitigation: Recorded in a shard.rs comment and in the design doc as something for the throughput review to watch. No grouping is done now; grouping a shard's units by package is the follow-up if recompile cost shows.

risks.risk: Shards are unbalanced, or one failing shard masks others.
risks.mitigation: Each shard runs all its units before exiting non-zero and names the failed ones. `fail-fast: false` keeps sibling shards running. A balance follow-up is recorded.

risks.risk: `ci` can go green before `pass` writes the marker, and `land`'s early wait (stale `EARLY_RUN_JOB`) ends at once, so a landing run can miss the cached pass and run the checks again.
risks.mitigation: `pass` is not required for `ci`, so a miss costs one extra run. The CHANGELOG entry and the design doc state it as a known effect and name the follow-up: target the marker-writing job, not `ci`.

risks.risk: A too-short `timeout-minutes` on a cold cache fails a legitimate run.
risks.mitigation: Compute jobs get a ceiling of about 30 minutes; the earlier whole run was about 16 minutes (D125 baseline), so a single job needs far less. The throughput review is the later check, and the values are labelled as ceilings.

risks.risk: New per-job target cache keys start cold, so the first runs after merge are slower.
risks.mitigation: Workflow comments and the design note say the first runs of the new keys miss. Only shard 0 saves the shared test key.

risks.risk: Editing policy.rs goes beyond the brief's deliverable list.
risks.mitigation: The edit is limited to re-pointing the two D121 tests (the reason is stated in the files list). The existing assertions are kept, not weakened.

demonstrations.method: Test `workflow_jobs_*` in xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs reads the real .github/workflows/ci.yml with std::fs, splits it into job blocks (two-space-indent keys under `jobs:`) and asserts: jobs `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` exist; `test` has `strategy.matrix.shard` of 6 entries; the job with `name: ci` has `needs` containing gate, fmt, clippy and test, has `if: always()`, and its run step exits 1 unless each need is success (or skipped when `gate.outputs.skip == 'true'`); every job block has `timeout-minutes`. Mutation checks on the text (remove `if: always()`, remove one `needs` entry, strip one `timeout-minutes`) are asserted to fail the same checks.
demonstrations.observes: The tests pass on the new ci.yml. Each mutated copy is rejected with a message naming the missing item.
demonstrations.fails_without: If ci.yml lacked the separate jobs, the 6-shard matrix, the `ci` job's needs/if: always()/result check, or any job's timeout-minutes, one of these tests fails.
demonstrations.seam: Reads the real repo file through std::fs with line regexes over job blocks; no double. Same style as the existing `checks_job_steps` in xtask/tests/policy.rs (exists). The new test file is added by plan step 6.

demonstrations.method: Re-pointed D121 tests in xtask/tests/policy.rs use `job_steps(job_id)`. In the gate job, fingerprint < lookup < decide, and the lookup is cache/restore with the fingerprint key. Each compute job has `needs: gate` and the skip condition. The `pass` job needs gate, fmt, clippy and test, has no always/failure/cancelled status, runs `ci-cache mark` then `cache/save` of `ci-pass` with no default-branch condition, and computes OUTCOME from the three results. The toolchain, registry and target saves in each compute job stay default-branch-only. In ci_shards.rs, `workflow_actions_are_pinned` asserts every `uses:` matches `@[0-9a-f]{40}`, and a test asserts fmt, clippy and test each restore the toolchain, registry and target caches.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p xtask --test policy && cargo test -p xtask --test ci_shards -- workflow_actions workflow_caches
demonstrations.observes: All pass. The existing policy assertions are kept, moved to the job that now holds each step.
demonstrations.fails_without: If a `uses:` were unpinned, a cache layer removed, the lookup/gate/mark steps dropped, or the mark/save steps given always() or a default-branch condition, the pinned-actions test or the re-pointed policy tests fail.
demonstrations.seam: Real ci.yml read via the helper in policy.rs, generalised from `checks_job_steps()` (exists) to `job_steps(job_id)` (plan step 7). `workflow_actions_are_pinned` and the cache test are added in step 6.

demonstrations.method: Test `shards_in_ci_yml_partition_every_workspace_test_target` calls `check_partition(real ci.yml text)`: parse the matrix list and n, run the built `xtask test-shard k n --dry-run` for each listed k, then `check_cover` against the independent cargo-metadata oracle; expect Ok. Negative tests, each asserted Err: (a) shape mutations of the ci.yml text (drop shard 5 from the list with n=6; duplicate a shard in the list; change the command's n to 5; each asserted to differ from the original). (b) Cover-only cases that pass the shape rule and call `check_cover` directly with real per-shard unit sets: one unit removed from its shard (error names it as missing), one unit copied into a second shard (error names it as duplicated), an oracle with one extra synthetic unit (error names it as missing from shards), and a shard unit absent from the oracle. A positive control checks `check_cover` returns Ok for the unmodified sets, so an always-Err or always-Ok comparison is caught either way.
demonstrations.observes: The positive test passes on the repository's ci.yml. Each negative case passes because it is rejected, and the cover-only ones are rejected by `check_cover` with the unit named in the error.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the cover comparison always returned Ok, the cover-only negative cases fail. If the shape rule were missing, the text-mutation cases fail. If the real shards missed or repeated a unit, the positive test fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: the built `xtask` binary, `test-shard <k> <n> --dry-run`, via `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_xtask")` (pattern in xtask/tests/fingerprint.rs, exists). Fixtures: the real ci.yml, in-memory mutated strings, and shard/oracle sets passed as arguments to the pure `check_cover` (added in step 6). The oracle is the test's own cargo metadata call plus the filesystem cross-check, with no logic imported from shard.rs. The subcommand and `--dry-run` are added by steps 2-4.

demonstrations.method: In ci_shards.rs, `test_shard_6_is_disjoint_and_equals_the_workspace_target_set` runs `test-shard k 6 --dry-run` for k in 0..=5 and asserts the unit lines are pairwise disjoint and their union equals the oracle. `test_shard_1_equals_the_workspace` does the same for n=1. `oracle_matches_files_on_disk` asserts every `src/lib.rs`, `tests/*.rs`, `src/main.rs` and `src/bin/*.rs` of each workspace member appears in the oracle. `test_shard_rejects_bad_arguments` runs `test-shard 6 6`, `0 0`, `3 2`, `x 6` and no arguments, asserts non-zero exit and an `error:`/usage message. Unit tests in shard.rs use a hand-written metadata JSON passed to `plan_units`: examples and benches are excluded; bin and test targets get `--bin`/`--test`; a lib with doctest=false has no `--doc` unit; `select` over n=1, 6 and n greater than the unit count is disjoint and complete. Local use: `cargo run -p xtask -- test-shard 0 6 --dry-run`.
demonstrations.observes: All xtask tests pass, including the existing ones. The dry-run output is a stable sorted list and the n shards together equal the workspace target set that `cargo test --workspace` runs.
demonstrations.fails_without: If `test-shard` were missing, selected overlapping units, left out any unit (for example doctests), or accepted k>=n or n=0, the disjoint/union test and the bad-argument test fail. If the oracle disagreed with the union of the n shards for n=1 or n=6, the union assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: the `xtask` binary (`main` dispatch to `shard::command`) run via CARGO_BIN_EXE_xtask against the real workspace. For unit tests, `shard::plan_units(&serde_json::Value)` takes the metadata JSON as an argument so a fixture is injected. Both are added by steps 2-4; the integration tests by step 6.

demonstrations.method: Run the three commands Athena runs, in order.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0. `cargo test --locked` also runs the new ci_shards tests and the re-pointed policy tests.
demonstrations.fails_without: A formatting difference, a clippy warning in shard.rs or the new tests, or a failing test (including the re-pointed policy tests) makes a command exit non-zero.
demonstrations.seam: The repository's own commands; no double.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff. An entry under `## [Unreleased]` names: the separate fmt, clippy and test jobs; the 6-shard matrix; the final `ci` gate job and its handling of a reused pass; the `pass` job that writes the D121 marker; `cargo run -p xtask -- test-shard <k> <n>` with `--dry-run`; the ci_shards partition test; the old check name `fmt, clippy, tests` that no longer exists (branch protection needs `ci`); and the known effect on `land`'s early-run wait (`EARLY_RUN_JOB` stale, so the landing run may miss the cached pass; follow-up should target the job that writes the marker).
demonstrations.observes: The entry exists and mentions each item.
demonstrations.fails_without: An empty CHANGELOG.md diff, or an entry missing one of the named items.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff. The ci.yml header comment, the CHANGELOG entry and the ci-routing.md section each say the run time of the new layout is not measured and is to be measured later by the throughput review. The only numbers quoted are the D125 baseline (about 16 minutes, labelled as the earlier measurement) and the timeout ceilings (labelled as ceilings, not measurements).
demonstrations.observes: No new timing is claimed; the throughput review is named as the later measure.
demonstrations.fails_without: Any text presenting a measured run time for the new layout would show as a minutes figure without a source in the diff.

open_questions: `EARLY_RUN_JOB` in crates/athena-core/src/gh/early.rs is "fmt, clippy, tests". After this change `land`'s early wait finds no such check run and ends at once. The follow-up should point it at the job that writes the marker (`pass`), or make `ci` wait for `pass`. Do the maintainers want that in this job? The plan leaves it out and records it as a known effect.
Branch protection must change from the old check name to `ci`. This is outside the repository, so the changelog states it.

Every compute job runs `./setup.sh --ci`, which builds xtask and athena in release mode. The code does not show whether fmt and clippy need it. The plan keeps it for fidelity and for the existing cache; the throughput review can judge it.

Index-modulo over target units can leave shards unbalanced, because one lib's tests (for example athena-core) cannot be split. Weighting by source size is a possible follow-up once real shard times exist.
ci.yml's matrix list and `test-shard` command shape are fixed by the regex parser. A later move to `include` or `fromJSON` makes the test fail loudly and the parser must be updated.
